title: Runtime-drift re-check: re-run every solutionVerified against updated pinned runtimes
context: open-coding-curriculum is an open CC-BY (prose) / MIT (code) curriculum of beginner programming lessons with graded, runnable exercises across languages. Every exercise carries a reference solution proven correct in CI (solutionVerified:true), learner code runs zero-install in-browser via WASM, and all content is machine-readable structured data so third parties can build on it. The project targets absolute beginners — self-learners, public-library patrons, under-resourced school students, career-changers — and operates under a donated-compute lane with no server-side execution of learner code and no partner confirmed yet (verifiedNeed:false). A Python or JavaScript version upgrade can silently break exercises that previously passed — the 'solutionVerified:true' badge becomes a lie. The runtime-drift re-check re-runs every reference solution against the current pinned runtimes and flags any newly failing exercise before it stays published with a stale verification.
objective: Re-run every exercise's reference solution against the current pinned runtime versions; identify and fix any exercise whose solution no longer passes; update pinned runtime version metadata.
acceptanceCriteria: Every exercise's reference solution is re-run against the current pinned Python and JavaScript runtime versions.
Any exercise whose reference solution no longer passes is flagged and fixed (solution updated or runtime version pinned/downgraded with documented rationale) before it can remain published.
Pinned runtime version metadata is updated for every exercise checked.
CI gate (occ-code-303) re-confirms solutionVerified:true for all exercises after the re-check.
The re-check results (pass count, failures found, fixes applied) are committed in a maintenance log.
output: A merged PR with updated runtime version metadata, fixed exercises (if any), and a maintenance log of the re-check results.
